name: Is my PDF uploaded anywhere to convert it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Table detection and spreadsheet generation both run in your browser using pdf.js and exceljs. Your PDF and the extracted data never leave your device.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.

name: What happens if my PDF has no tables?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree tells you before you convert — the pre-scan badge shows the table count. If none are found, every line of text still gets saved into a single 'Text' sheet, but for prose-heavy documents, PDF to Word is usually a better fit.

name: Can I convert a scanned PDF to Excel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not directly — a scanned PDF is an image with no text layer, so there's no data to detect a table in. Run OCR PDF first to add a text layer, then convert the result to Excel.

name: How does PDFree know what's a table and what isn't?

acceptedAnswer.text: It checks whether text lines line up into consistent columns across at least 3 rows. Each candidate gets a confidence score; low-confidence guesses are rejected rather than shown as a broken table.

name: Is this a free PDF to Excel converter with no sign up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree is completely free — no sign up, no account, no installation. Open the tool, load your PDF, and download the .xlsx file.

name: Can I edit the formulas or recalculate after converting?

acceptedAnswer.text: The extracted values are plain numbers and text, not formulas — a PDF has no underlying formulas to recover, only rendered results. Once in Excel, you can add your own formulas over the extracted data as usual.

name: If my PDF has multiple tables, do they end up on separate sheets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each detected table becomes its own sheet in the output .xlsx file, named and ordered to match its position in the PDF, so tables from different pages or sections don't get mixed together.
